summary: Explains `throttle`, set on a block or task, to limit workers for CPU-intensive tasks or rate-limited APIs. It can only lower parallelism below `forks` or `serial`, not raise it.
questions: How do I make one task run on only one host at a time?
How do I avoid hitting an API rate limit from many hosts?
Can throttle be higher than forks?
Can I set throttle on a block?

answer_card.title: Restrict a task with throttle
answer_card.answer_md:
`throttle` limits the number of workers for a task or block, useful for CPU-intensive commands or rate-limited APIs:
```yaml
tasks:
  - command: /path/to/cpu_intensive_command
    throttle: 1
```
It can only **reduce** parallelism: to have an effect it must be lower than your `forks` or `serial` setting.
